finding: findAvailablePorts bind-check: on a bindable-fail path releasePortLock is correctly called before continue, and the happy path returns the base pair unchanged. Verified by TEST-1 (happy) + TEST-2 (skip to +8). No lock leak.

The isPortBindable check is inherently TOCTOU (a sibling could bind between our close() and the server's later listen). This is the SAME accepted window as the sibling allocatePostgresPort and is documented; it strictly reduces (does not eliminate) collisions. By-design, matches precedent.
killProcessOnPort wraps each external call in try/catch and hasCmd swallows a missing-tool throw; the no-tool case now warns instead of silently no-opping. No unhandled reject. Adequate.

Command-injection review of the execSync shell strings: `command -v ${cmd}` uses only hardcoded literals ('lsof'/'fuser'/'ss'); `fuser -k ${port}/tcp` and `ss ... :${port}` interpolate a numeric port from arithmetic (never user/model input). No injection surface.
win32 arm (netstat/taskkill) preserved byte-for-byte in both copies; fuser/ss fallbacks are gated behind the non-win32 branch, so Windows behavior is unchanged. Parity maintained.

Test hygiene: TEST-2 closes both held listeners in finally; releasePortLock is called for every returned pair; temp bin/config dirs and the extra postgres lock are rmSync'd in finally. No leaked listeners/locks/dirs across tests.

killProcessOnPort logic is now duplicated (win32 + lsof/fuser/ss chain) across port-manager.ts and test-context.ts. Pre-existing duplication (two independent copies predate this change); extracting a shared helper would couple test-context's dynamic-import shape to port-manager. Acceptable; noted for a future DRY pass, not blocking.

Assertions genuinely prove the claims: TEST-2 asserts the exact +8 offset (deterministic, not just 'not base'); TEST-3 is hermetic (PATH-scoped fake bins, asserts the recorded `-k <port>/tcp` args and that lsof is preferred); TEST-4 uses real files+locks. No always-true/cosmetic asserts.
Newly-exported helpers (killProcessOnPort, extractConfigId, collectLiveRunIds) have clear names + doc-comments; signatures are pure and hard to misuse. Additive export, no call-site churn.

cleanupStaleConfigFiles live-lock guard reuses the exact liveRunIds idiom from global-setup.ts (postgres-*.lock -> process.kill(pid,0)); findAvailablePorts mirrors allocatePostgresPort. Conformant with in-repo precedent.

The lsof->fuser->ss chain is an ordered if/hasCmd ladder; adding another tool is a localized new branch. extractConfigId centralizes filename->id mapping so a new run-scoped file type is one line. Reasonable seams.

collectLiveRunIds is a self-contained reader over the shared lock dir with a narrow boundary; the config sweep and container sweep now share the same liveness contract without cross-coupling. Change is contained to the harness module.

BLIND-AUDIT: the stale-lock REAP paths (cleanupStaleLocks + acquirePortLock's stale branch) still call killProcessOnPort(port) with no bind/ownership guard, so a crashed prior run's stale lock in OUR dir can trigger a kill of a LIVE sibling now holding that base port. Real residual of the same class.
status: deferred-out-of-scope: the authoritative reference fix scopes fix #1 to findAvailablePorts ONLY; the reap-path hardening is a DISTINCT change because a leaked-orphan (which SHOULD be reaped) is indistinguishable from a live sibling by a bind-probe alone (and lsof is absent on the box). Recorded as a follow-up in HUMAN_FEEDBACK; the PRIMARY victim path (allocation + test-context self-kill) IS fixed.

finding: BLIND-AUDIT: the test-context copy of killProcessOnPort had NO final else, so it still silently no-opped when no tool exists — inconsistent with the port-manager copy and contrary to fix #2's goal.
status: confirmed-fixed: added the final else warn (mirrors port-manager copy).

finding: BLIND-AUDIT: TEST-3 writes #!/bin/sh fakes + chmod exec bit + command -v; incompatible with Windows test:unit and had no skip.
status: confirmed-fixed: added { skip: process.platform === 'win32' } — a legitimate platform gate (the win32 arm of killProcessOnPort is unchanged), not a go-green skip.

finding: BLIND-AUDIT: TEST-2's hard `=== V+8` equality flakes if another process grabs the +8 offset between probe and allocation. ALSO: node --test corrupted its IPC intermittently (Unable to deserialize cloned data) due to the verbose emoji stdout interleaving on the runner pipe.
status: confirmed-fixed: relaxed to a robust skip-invariant (not-held-base + forward-by-a-multiple-of-8 + same-offset-both) AND silenced console in the spec. Verified 25/25 stable runs after the fix.

finding: BLIND-AUDIT: killProcessOnPort interpolates port into shell strings; port ultimately reads from JSON lock files, so a corrupted lock could carry a non-numeric string. Not widened beyond the pre-existing lsof/netstat surface.
status: confirmed-fixed: added a `Number.isInteger(port) && port>0` guard at the top of both copies before any interpolation (defense-in-depth).

finding: BLIND-AUDIT (leg B): claimed the fake lsof prints 'called' to stdout so production runs `kill -9 called`.
status: rejected-false-positive: the fake lsof uses `echo called > "$marker"` which redirects to the marker FILE, leaving stdout EMPTY, so the production lsof arm sees no output and returns early — no `kill -9 called` runs. Verified by the passing test.

status: confirmed-fixed: added the explicit TOCTOU caveat to the comment (strongly reduces, cannot fully eliminate) for doc honesty.
